findings.mechanism: Pins 1 and 2 are transposed at the external interface. A harness built per the contract drives the source into the R1/C1 junction (directly loading the source with C1, no defined series element) and takes 'output' from the far end of R1, so the specified input-at-pin-2, filtered-output-at-pin-1 behavior is not delivered; the sole stated acceptance criterion fails. The error is invisible to ERC/DRC/schematic parity because schematic and board are mutually consistent — net names simply attach the roles to the wrong pins.
findings.reasoning: Three independent derivations agree: (1) geometric reconstruction of J1's pin positions under its saved 180-degree rotation maps pin 1 to the wire labeled 'IN' and pin 2 to 'OUT'; (2) a fresh kicad-cli netlist export reproduces /IN=[J1.1,R1.1] and /OUT=[C1.1,J1.2,R1.2]; (3) pcbnew reads the same pad-net assignments from the board, and the copper implements them. Electrically the net on J1.1 is unambiguously the filter input (it reaches only the free end of series R1) and the net on J1.2 is the filtered R-C node, so this is a true role swap at the connector, not a naming quibble. It directly violates the only evaluated criterion, which supports blocking severity; schematic and board agree with each other, so the fix is a design change (reassign J1 pins 1/2), not a layout parity repair.

findings.mechanism: ERC/DRC/parity verify internal self-consistency (schematic vs board, copper rules), not requirement-level pin assignments. A pin-role swap propagated consistently through schematic and layout produces zero findings; a successful tool exit is then mistaken for contract compliance unless a dedicated assertion (e.g. expected net name per J1 pad number) is run against the netlist or geometry output.
findings.reasoning: This is a verification-coverage observation, not a tool failure: the tools ran correctly and their outputs are reproducible (I re-ran the netlist export with identical results). The gap is that the declared criteria (erc, drc, netlist, geometry) contain no assertion binding net /IN to J1 pad 2 and /OUT to J1 pad 1 per the contract, so green results provide no evidence for the one requirement under review. Flagged as a concern so the harness adds a pin-role assertion; severity minor because the data needed for such a check is already produced by the existing netlist/geometry evidence.
findings.title: Criteria set cannot detect the connector-contract violation: all native checks pass on an internally consistent but contract-swapped design
